text:
maria: Heads up — we've been seeing short bursts of link resets and elevated RX errors on g7u instances in us-west-2 starting ~15:30 PDT. East-west traffic shows intermittent 1-3% packet loss during the spikes. Posting quick logs below.

maria: ethtool -S eth0 output (trimmed):
```
rx_errors: 1245
rx_crc_errors: 0
rx_no_buffer: 0
rx_missed_frames: 0
tx_errors: 3
tx_dropped: 0
link_reset_count: 5
```

ryan: ack. Can you paste a couple affected instance IDs + AZ? Is this limited to one AZ or across the region?

maria: instances: i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 (us-west-2b), i-0b2c3d4e5f6a78901 (us-west-2b). Control plane/other fleets in 2a/2c look fine.

oleg: seeing similar kernel messages on one host earlier: dmesg excerpt:
```
[12345.678901] ixgbe 0000:81:00.0 eth0: Reset request due to link change, reset_count=4
[12345.679012] ixgbe 0000:81:00.0: NIC hw watchdog: resetting
[12345.679123] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: PME# disabled
```

tasha: quick checklist: any recent driver/firmware rollouts in the AZ? MTU mismatch between hosts/switch? Offloads? Can you run `ethtool -k eth0` and `ip link show dev eth0` on one of the affected boxes?

maria: ethtool -k eth0 (partial):
```
Offload parameters for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tso: on
gro: on
lro: off
```
ip link shows MTU 9000 on the host. Switch side shows 1500 for the same VLAN (still confirming).

infra-bot: [ALERT] net-telemetry: Increased rx_errors and link resets on g7u fleet in us-west-2b (see graphs) — https://grafana.internal/r/abc123

ryan: if switch MTU != host MTU that can cause fragmentation and link anomalies under bursty traffic. But driver resets point at possible firmware regression. Any recent firmware tags pushed?

oleg: vendor report shows a g7u firmware pushed two weeks ago (fw v2.2.0). We were on 2.1.5 previously. I want to validate by rolling a canary back to 2.1.5 on one host.

tasha: also try toggling GSO/TSO off for a test to see if offload aggregation is triggering the issue: `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` — instrument with tcpdump and counters before/after.

maria: running `sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off` now on i-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890. Will capture pcap: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/capture.pcap` and collect counters every 30s.

oleg: good. If turning off offloads stabilizes traffic, that strongly points to driver/firmware interaction. We should prepare a rollback to 2.1.5 and coordinate with networking team for switch MTU check.

ryan: mitigation plan proposal:
- Step 1: Canaries — pick 2 hosts in 2b, disable offloads, monitor 30m.
- Step 2: If stable, schedule driver/firmware rollback for affected AZ during 02:00-04:00 PDT maintenance window.
- Step 3: If rollback not possible, keep offloads off and throttle e2e traffic as emergency fallback.

maria: can do canary now. Running tcpdump + counters. Will post results in ~20m.

infra-bot: [NOTIFICATION] maintenance-window created: rollback-plan-g7u-1749948765 (owner: oleg) — scheduled 2025-03-18 02:00 PDT.

oleg: I'll open a vendor TAC case with the firmware vendor and attach the tcpdump + dmesg, reference internal bug INF-3217.

sre-oncall: please add a short runbook snippet to the ticket for rollback steps and verification checks. Quick template:
```
1) coord ops -> cordon hosts
2) drain non-critical pods
3) stop services that pin NICs
4) flash fw v2.1.5 via vendor utility (safe-mode)
5) reboot and verify ethtool -S counters stable for 10m
6) re-enable offloads and test throughput
```

maria: added runbook snippet to INF-3217. After disabling offloads on canaries, rx_errors held steady for 20m. No new link_reset_count bumps so far.

ryan: that's encouraging. Tasha, can your team confirm switch MTU config and any auto-negotiation differences for the VLAN?

tasha: pinged networking team on #network-ops and awaiting confirmation. They asked for port list; I've sent switch ports for the two hosts.

oleg: moving forward: I'll keep the vendor case open, coordinate rollback steps, and run the canary rollback if networking confirms MTU consistent.

maria: thanks everyone — will update once capture + counters finish (next ping ~15:55 PDT). :thumbsup:

ryan: thx. react with :white_check_mark: when you have the pcap attached.

maria: attached /tmp/capture.pcap to INF-3217 and set last checks. No further link resets on canaries in the last 30m. Closing fast-response for now, keeping ticket open for rollout.

sre-oncall: noted. Marking as monitoring.

oleg: vendor TAC replied — they acknowledged a regression in fw v2.2.0 for ixgbe-like silicon under certain jumbo frames and offload combos. They recommended rollback to 2.1.5. I'll coordinate the rollout with ops and networking.

maria: copy. Planning rollback in the scheduled window. Thanks. :party_parrot:
